A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe KL/SoftPlus approximation work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable. The original appendices can be matched despite v4 inserting a new DRO appendix and renumbering later appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original continuous-OT and DRO experiments in Section 3, Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3, plus kernel-based OT experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original distribution-shift, synthetic regression and severe-label-noise results in Appendix C, Tables 3–5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 newly specifies a projected stochastic-subgradient procedure for the convex parametric case, including a bounded interval for alpha, a prescribed stepsize and iterate averaging. The Safe KL surrogate, application-specific estimators and experimental architectures remain unchanged; the shift in alpha notation is equivalent.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds ACS PUMS income prediction under California–Mississippi distribution shift, synthetic linear-regression data, and an 85%-label-noise MNIST scenario alongside the retained 25%-noise experiment. These substantially extend the represented populations and evaluation conditions.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain LSOT, Genevay et al.'s kernel OT method, Levy et al.'s KL-DRO estimator and Wang et al.'s UOT-DRO approach. The added benchmark comparisons reuse the corresponding DRO baselines. Newly cited compositional optimization methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained, but Appendix C introduces substantial new protocols: asymmetric state splits, race-group RMSE/MAE, exact duality-gap evaluation through weighted least squares, and downstream classification metrics. Table 5 selects each metric's best value separately across gamma/lambda settings, including separately optimized hardest-class metrics.

E4.justification: v4 adds tests of robustness to population shift and severe label corruption, including whether lower DRO objectives translate into better overall and worst-group predictions. Appendix C.2 also adds an exact duality-gap analysis of optimization progress, supplementing the retained objective-value and parameter-sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: New Figure 6 reports means over five seeds with minimum-to-maximum shading, introducing an uncertainty display different from the standard-deviation bands used in the retained convergence plots. Existing experiments retain their stated run counts and uncertainty reporting; no increase in their runs is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original figures retain their results, while Tables 3–5 and Figure 6 add substantial findings. New ACS objectives include 109.3±0.4 for the baseline versus 106.0±0.9 at rho=10^-3. Under 85% noise, Table 5's best-over-settings results show proposed/baseline cross-entropy of 1.29±0.08/1.36±0.03 but accuracy of 0.34±0.02/0.41±0.04. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v3 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Proposition 2.4(iii) replaces the earlier linear error bound with a sharper logarithmic bound and extends its admissible rho range. Assumption 2.8, Theorem 2.9 and its Appendix A proof add a finite-iteration optimization guarantee. v4 also corrects the reversed approximation inequalities and the missing exponential in Corollary 2.5's proof.

C1.justification: Contribution 3 narrows 'outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines' to 'competitive performance' against representative application-specific baselines. The introduction also replaces broad absence-of-method assertions with qualified discussion of sampled-estimator bias. The central Safe KL approximation and convexity/smoothness claims remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly cautions that KL-specific structural properties may require separate analysis and explicitly identifies parameter tuning and limited task coverage as limitations. Appendix C connects objective values to downstream prediction while acknowledging that the baseline achieves higher overall accuracy under severe label noise.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds ACS data-source and split information, parameters for the new studies, and synthetic sample size and dimension. Tables 3 and 5 add time-per-epoch measurements. Existing architecture descriptions, hyperparameter grids and the code-access disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantive positioning against stochastic compositional optimization, discussing Qi et al. (2021, 2023), Wang and Yang (2022), and Yuan et al. (2022). It presents Safe KL as complementary to optimizers for the original objective, replacing v3's broader lack-of-universal-method framing. This materially revises the novelty context.

P1.justification: v4 makes targeted rewrites to the introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion, expands Section 2.2, and standardizes terminology and headings. It adds acknowledgements and Appendix C, moving the existing SoftPlus and LLM-disclosure appendices to D and E. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the empirical displays with Tables 3–5 covering regression, worst-group performance, severe-noise objectives, classification and runtime, plus a logarithmic duality-gap plot in Figure 6. Figures 1–5 retain identical embedded graphics, and Tables 1–2 retain their structures; these original displays mainly undergo page reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important gaps in v3 by adding an optimization guarantee under explicit assumptions, strengthening and correcting mathematical reasoning, and testing downstream robustness beyond objective minimization. The revised literature positioning and narrower claims improve reliability. The new evidence does not establish uniform superiority: Table 5 selects metrics across settings and reports lower overall accuracy and higher runtime for the proposed method. These qualifications limit the performance claims but do not outweigh the substantial gains in theoretical support and empirical assessment.
